name: Polyisobutylene (PIB): The Invisible Guardian of Modern Glass

density.conditions: 20°C, amorphous, high-MW PIB (Mark; matches the formula 0.9171-30/Mn extrapolated to high Mn); Wypych reports 0.788-0.921 across the oligomer MW range, 0.972 crystalline; Mark separately reports crystalline density 0.964

refractive_index.conditions: 20°C, high-MW PIB; oligomers range lower at 1.445-1.508; Mark's high-Mn extrapolated value is 1.5092

electrical_conductivity.conditions: 20°C, gum vulcanizate; reported directly as conductivity, not as the reciprocal of resistivity

water_absorption.conditions: <200 ppm (<0.02%), pure polymer, 20°C, total immersion; compounding increases uptake

synthesis.industrial_process_notes: Made via cationic polymerization initiated by a strong Bronsted or Lewis acid. Low molecular weight grades (Mn ~500) serve as plasticizers; medium/high molecular weight grades (Mn >= 20,000) go into adhesives. Copolymerization with a small amount of isoprene gives butyl rubber (a distinct, separately-tracked material).

structure_morphology.chain_flexibility_notes: Fully saturated, methyl-substituted backbone gives PIB very low gas permeability and excellent chemical inertness -- the properties underlying its 'invisible sealant' role in insulating glass.

mn.conditions: oligomer range (Wypych); Mark gives a wider application-dependent range: 500-5,000 (dispersants) up to 5,000-6,000,000 (blends/viscosity modifiers/chewing gum), 100,000-600,000 (elastomer grades)

k.conditions: PIB/IIR chapter (isobutylene homopolymer and its <1% isoprene copolymer reported together for this dilute-solution property)

tg.conditions: exp.; calc.=-71; Mark's DSC measurement gives -71°C and -65°C (202 K, 208 K), consistent

tm.conditions: PIB crystallizes below 20°C or under mechanical stress; Mark reports melting points of 275 K and 317 K (~2°C and ~44°C, depending on annealing conditions) for this stress-/cold-crystallized form, with a heat of fusion of 52 cal/g at the melting point -- not a melt transition of the material in its normal amorphous gum state.

tc.conditions: PIB is capable of crystallizing below 20°C or under mechanical stress (see tm), but neither handbook reports a numeric crystallization temperature.

hdt.conditions: No ASTM D648 heat-deflection-under-load result exists for this uncrosslinked gum elastomer; Mark separately reports a low-temperature deflection value of <210 K (<-63°C) tied to its glass transition (202-208 K), a different quantity from heat deflection under load.

decomposition_onset.conditions: >120°C; Mark reports 50% volatile loss in 30 min at 320°C (a different, less conservative degradation metric)

thermal_conductivity.conditions: 20°C, gum vulcanizate; rises to 0.23 with 50 phr carbon black filler; Wypych separately reports 0.19-0.26 for the melt

tensile_modulus.conditions: Uncrosslinked PIB gum has no stable equilibrium tensile modulus in the conventional solid sense; Mark's only reported figure (0.5-50 MPa) is explicitly stated to depend on compounding ingredients, i.e. it describes compounded/vulcanized rubber rather than the neat homopolymer.

yield_strength.conditions: Elastomeric stress-strain behavior shows no distinct yield point; neither handbook reports one.

tensile_strength_at_break.conditions: excludes Mark's much broader compounded-rubber range (0.5-50 MPa), which reflects filled/vulcanized IIR formulations rather than neat PIB

impact_izod.conditions: Notched Izod impact testing requires a rigid molded bar; not meaningful for an uncrosslinked gum elastomer, and neither handbook reports a value.

impact_charpy.conditions: Notched Charpy impact testing requires a rigid molded bar; not meaningful for an uncrosslinked gum elastomer, and neither handbook reports a value.

hardness.conditions: Uncrosslinked, unvulcanized PIB gum lacks the stable elastic network a durometer reading needs; Mark's only reported figure (Shore A 5-100) is explicitly compounding-dependent, reflecting finished vulcanized rubber goods rather than the neat homopolymer.

flexural_modulus.conditions: Three-point flexural testing requires a rigid bar specimen; not meaningful for an uncrosslinked gum elastomer, and neither handbook reports a value.

weathering_uv.value: Degrades via ozone attack and UV-driven autoxidation (hydroperoxides, chain scission, crosslinking); no stabilizer-based photostability class given

hydrolysis_resistance.conditions: Fully saturated hydrocarbon backbone (isobutylene units only); no hydrolyzable linkages.

processing_temp_range.conditions: Fabricated by compounding, vulcanization, coating and sheeting rather than thermoplastic melt processing; neither handbook reports a processing temperature range.

shrinkage_rate.conditions: Not injection-molded into rigid parts (fabricated by compounding/coating/sheeting instead), so mold shrinkage is not a meaningful measurement; neither handbook reports a value.

nfpa_health_rating.conditions: HMIS rating, 0-4 scale (health reported as a 0-1 range)

carcinogenic_classification.value: not listed by ACGIH, NIOSH, NTP

toxicity_safety.safety_notes: TLV (ACGIH): 2 mg/m³ inhalable. Skin (rabbit) LD50: non-irritant. Mutagenic, teratogenic and reproductive toxicity: none reported.
